title: R' Yosi bar Kesariy
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.4), he disagrees with Rabbi Tanchuma over “Of the sons of Issachar, who understood the times”: R' Yosi bar Kesariy says that this refers to calendar intercalations. The saying is repeated in Bamidbar Rabbah 13:16, where he is called only Rabbi Yosi, with bar Kesariy omitted. At the beginning of Esther Rabbah, chapter 4, the reading is Rabbi Yosi bar Katzrat, which should read bar Kesariy. In Bereshit Rabbah 22:14, Abba Yosi ben Kisri says, “He caused a horn to grow” (for Cain). See the entry R' Yosi of Kesari.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The earlier Katzet omitted a resh from קצרת; Katzrat retains the supplied consonants without claiming an established vocalization. שהש״ר, במ״ר, אס״ר and ב״ר are rendered by the ordinary/contextual titles Shir HaShirim Rabbah, Bamidbar Rabbah, Esther Rabbah and Bereshit Rabbah; ב״ק is bar Kesariy from the full name already given, not Bava Kamma. The place/name forms Kesariy, Katzrat and Kisri are kept distinct. The parenthetic Cain is Hyman’s; the pronoun “He” is not given a newly invented antecedent. The proposed correction and the cross-reference remain Hyman’s claims, not independently verified identities.

The checked Midrash Rabbah -- TE text of Esther Rabbah 4:1 explicitly has Rabbi Tanchuma and Rabbi Yosi bar Katzrat discussing this Issachar verse. The corresponding saying is found in that edition’s [Bamidbar Rabbah 13:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Bamidbar_Rabbah.13.15), rather than the printed 13:16 cited by Hyman; it explicitly names Rabbi Yosi without a patronymic. The horn saying is at [Bereshit Rabbah 22:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.22.12) in this edition, rather than Hyman’s 22:14, and names Abba Yosi ben Kesari. The printed locators and Hyman’s Kisri form are retained in the translation; these edition differences are not silently repaired. The exact claimed Shir HaShirim Rabbah passage was not located in the bounded chapter check, and Hyman’s proposed Katzrat/Kesariy identification is not proved by the Esther passage. The heading, the Kesariy attribution and the cross-reference to Yosi of Kesari therefore retain neutral R'; no title is transferred from a proposed identification. The titles Rabbi Tanchuma, Rabbi Yosi and Rabbi Yosi bar Katzrat are explicit in the matching checked reports.
